nodes.name: Theorem 1.2, Section 3: norm variation estimate three transformations
Proposition 2.3, Section 5: Prop Sect on-diagonal non-Whitney 2D
nodes.statement:
[Proved in Section 5]
There exists $C>0$ such that the following holds. 
Let $J$ be a positive integer and   $(k_j)_{j=1}^J$ and $(l_j)_{j=1}^J$   two finite sequences of integers  that are interlaced in the sense that $k_{j}+10< l_j$ for $1\le j\le J$ and
$l_j< k_{j+1}$ for $1\le j<J-1$.
Consider a kernel
\[K=\sum_{j=1}^J ({\phi}_{0,j}-{\phi}_{1,j})\otimes  ({\phi}_{0,j}-{\phi}_{1,j}),\]
where, for each $j$,
${(\phi_{0,j})_{(2^{-k_j})}}$ is a left window 
and ${(\phi_{1,j})_{(2^{-l_j})}}$ is a right window.

Then estimate (2.2) holds for any tuple as in (2.3), (2.4).

nodes.name: Proposition 2.1, Section 4: Prop Sect on-diagonal Whitney 2D
nodes.statement:
[Proved in Section 4]
Let $\lambda=\frac{3}{2}$.
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds for all $k \leq 0$. 
Let $J$ be a positive integer and   $(k_j)_{j=1}^J$ 
  a finite strictly monotone increasing sequence of integers.
Let
\[K =\sum_{j=1}^J \Phi_j,\]
where for each $1\le j\le J$ we assume 
$\Phi_j$ is a real valued  function on ${\mathbb R}^2$,
with symmetry $$\Phi_j(u,v)=\Phi_j(v,u)$$ and positivity
in the sense
\begin{equation}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^2} f(u)\overline{f(v)}\Phi_j(u,v)\,dudv\ge 0
\end{equation}
for all complex-valued $f$.
We assume further
\begin{equation*}
{\rm supp} (\widehat{\Phi_j})\subset 
([-2^{-k_j+20},-2^{-k_j-20}]\cup [2^{-k_j-20},2^{-k_j+20}])^2
\end{equation*}  
and, for all $(u,v)\in {\mathbb R}^2$,
\begin{equation}
 |(\Phi_j)_{(2^{-k_j})}(u, v)| \leq  2^{\lambda k}(1+2^k|u+v|)^{-10} (1+|u-v|)^{-10}.
\end{equation}
Then estimate (2.2) holds for any tuple as in (2.3), (2.4).

nodes.name: Proposition 2.5, Section 6: Prop Sect off-diagonal Whitney 2D
nodes.statement:
[Proved in Section 6]  
Let $\lambda=\frac{3}{2}$. There exists a constant $C>0$  such that the following holds for all $k\leq 0$. Let $J$ be a positive integer and let $(k_j)_{j=1}^J$ be a finite 
strictly increasing sequence of integers. Let $(\Phi_j)_{j=1}^J$ be a finite sequence of real valued functions on ${\mathbb R}^2$.
Assume that 
\[\textup{supp}(\widehat{\Phi_j}) \subseteq \{(\xi,\eta)\in {\mathbb R}^2 : 2^{-k_{j}-30}\leq |(\xi,\eta)| \leq 2^{-k_j+30} \}.  \]
Assume further that  for all $(u,v)\in {\mathbb R}^2$, 
\begin{equation}
|(\Phi_j)_{(2^{-k_j})}(u,v)| \leq  2^{\lambda k}(1+2^k|u+v|)^{-4} (1+|u-v|)^{-4} 
+(1+|u+v|)^{-4} (1+|u-v|)^{-4}.
\end{equation}
Let $K$ be defined by
\[
K=\sum_{j=1}^J \Phi_{j}
\]
and assume that $\widehat{K}$ vanishes on the diagonal $\{(\xi,\eta)\in {\mathbb R}^2: \xi+\eta=0\}$.

Then estimate (2.2) holds for any tuple as in (2.3), (2.4).

nodes.name: Proposition 2.6, Section 7: Prop Sect off-diagonal non-Whitney 2D
nodes.statement:
[Proved in Section 7] 
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds.
Let $J$ be a positive integer and $(k_j)_{j=0}^J$   a   finite increasing sequence of integers with $k_{j-1}+10 \le k_{j}$
for $1\le j \leq J$. 
For $1\le j\le J$,  let $\phi_{0,j}$, $\phi_{1,j}$, $\phi_{2,j}$
be functions such that
${(\phi_{0,j})_{(2^{-k_{j-1}})}}$ is a left window, while
${(\phi_{1,j})_{(2^{-k_j})}}$  and 
${(\phi_{2,j})_{(2^{4-k_j})}}$ are right windows.
Define 
\begin{equation}
K = \sum_{j=1}^J (\phi_{0,j}-\phi_{2,j})\otimes  \phi_{1,j} .  
\end{equation} 

Then estimate (2.2) holds for any tuple as in (2.3), (2.4).

nodes.name: Proposition 2.7, Section 8: Prop Sect on-critical non-Whitney 3D
nodes.statement:
[Proved in Section 8]
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds.
Let $\alpha\ge 1$. Let $J$ be a positive integer and $(k_j)_{j=0}^J$   a   finite increasing sequence of integers with $k_{j-1}+10 \leq k_{j}$ for $1\le j \leq J$. Let $(m_j)_{j=1}^J$ be a sequence of real numbers with
$k_j-1\le m_j\le k_j$ for $1\le j\le J$.  For $0\le j\le J$, let $\chi_j$
be a function such that ${(\chi_j)_{(2^{2-k_j})}}$ is a left window
and let $\phi_{j}$ be such that $\widehat{\phi_j} \geq 0$ and
$$ (\widehat{\phi_{j}})^2=(\widehat{\chi_{j-1}})^2-
(\widehat{\chi_{j}})^2.$$
Let
\begin{equation*}
K(u,v,z)=\alpha^{-N} \sum_{j=1}^J \int_{{\mathbb R}}g_{(\alpha 2^{m_j})}(u+p) g_{(\alpha 2^{m_j})}(v+p)
 {\phi}_{j}(z+p){\phi}_{j}(p)  \, dp.
\end{equation*}

Then estimate (2.11) holds for any tuple as in (2.12), (2.13).

nodes.name: Proposition 2.8, Section 9.1: Prop Sect off-critical non-Whitney 3D discrete
nodes.statement:
[Proved in Section 9]
 
 There is a constant $C$ such that the following holds. Let $J$ be a positive integer. 
For $1\le i\le 2$,  let  $(a_{i,j})_{j=1}^{J}$  be increasing sequences of positive real numbers. 


For $1\leq j \leq J$,  let $\rho_{j}:{\mathbb R}^4\to {\mathbb R}$ be a continuous function satisfying 

\begin{equation}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^2} |\rho_{j} | (u_1+p,u_2+p,u_3+r,u_4+r)\, dp dr
 \le a_{1,j}^{-1}(1+a_{1,j}^{-1}|u_1-u_2|)^{-2}
 a_{2,j}^{-1}(1+a_{2,j}^{-1}|u_3-u_4|)^{-2}
\end{equation}
for every $(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4)\in {\mathbb R}^4$.
Let $(c_j)_{j=0}^J$ be an increasing sequence of positive {real} numbers,
well separated in that $2c_{j-1}\le c_j$ for $1\le j\le J$.
 Let $\chi$ be a left window.
For $1\le j\le J$ let $\phi_{j}:{\mathbb R}\to {\mathbb R}$ be   a continuous function, which exists due
 to the left window property of $\chi$, satisfying  $\widehat{\phi_j} \geq 0$  and 
 \[(\widehat{\phi_{j}})^2 = (\widehat{{\chi}_{(c_{j-1})}})^2 
 - (\widehat{{\chi}_{(c_j)}})^2. \]
 Let $K$ be defined by   
      \begin{equation}
        
    {K}(u,v,z)= \sum_{j=1}^J \int_{{\mathbb R}^3}{\phi_{j}}(p)
    {\phi_{j}}(q) {\rho_{j}}(u+p+q+r,v+p+q+r,z+r,r) \,dpdqdr. 
    \end{equation}

      Then estimate (2.11) holds for any tuple as in (2.12), (2.13).
